YMCA'S EDUCATION PROGRAMES 
SUBJECT/SUJET__LOOSEN MACHINE AGE SHACKLES

POUR RENSEIGNEMENTS 
COMMUNIQUER Avec WILLIAM SHER 


[CONTACT 


Emphasis of the Montreal YMCA's fall education program is on 
courses which tap and develop individual capacities to enjoy 


more things more fully. 


Many of these simultaneously stretch participants! abilities 
to cope with the accelerating tempo of change and the 


dehumanizing forces of our machine-oriented society. 


At the Downtown, NDG and Westmount branches, courses start 
October 9. They range from speed reading, bridge playing, drama, 
public speaking, creative writing, painting and dancing through 


dressmaking, languages and industrial management. 


“While not a panacea, continuing education can help cure a number 
of social ills and point the way to solutions for many others," 
says R.D. Sallery, adult program director of the Downtown YMCA. 


Continued 


"Unfortunately, too many of us tend to equate learning with 
childhood. We try to make education universal for youngsters and, 


in doing so, frequently assume it is only for them." 


He suggested that, in the minds of many adults, enrollment in 
any sort of course of study is tantamount to an admission of 


inadequacy. 


"That's nonsense. These days, willingness to continue learning is 


almost the only answer to obsolescence," he insists. 


Mr. Sallery suggests that the present structure of society tends to 


trap individuals at minimal levels of performance and achievements. 


Continued 


As a result, most people use only a small percentage of their 


potential capacities. 


"Continuing education, adult education, creative use of leisure 


time -- call it what you like -- can help an individual live 


up to his potential and enjoy it," comments Mr. Sallery. 


-30- 


September 25, 1967.
